The petitioners filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Channagangaiah, in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 12.2.2020.

Due to the impact the deceased sustained injuries and fell on the road, at the same time another motor bike deo vehicle which was also being ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.

33 . It must be understood that no doubt the police have charge sheeted the rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-49-H-2462, but this court is not bound by the Sunanda vs Renuka B Killari on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28063228/

Merely because all the police papers point towards the fact that the motor cycle bearing No.
KA-49-H-2462 belonging to the respondent No.1 was involved in the accident in which the deceased sustained the injuries and succumbed to the injuries, this court is not bound to accept the same.

Because in the present  SCCH-17 31 MVC 1320/2021 case, except mahazar no other documents or evidence placed before the tribunal to show the involvement of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-49-H-2462 in the accident.

At this juncture, it is to be noted that the law is settled on the point regarding assessment and evaluation of negligence by Accident Claims Tribunal and it is well- settled principle of law that the Accident Claim Tribunal should independently evaluate and assess the materials placed before it in order to come to a conclusion regarding rashness and negligence not being influenced by police papers or the result of criminal case.

No doubt in this case the insurance company has not challenged the charge sheet filed by the police,

21 regarding non involvement of the the motor cycle bearing No. KA-49-H-2462 is proved.

This is because, as already observed above, the involvement of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-49-H-2462 is itself doubtful and secondly no eye witness is examined by the petitioners to support their contention.

35 . Further it is necessary to note that law is well settled in this regard that irrespective of whether the driver of the alleged vehicle involved in the accident pleads guilty, the court can still appreciate the facts independently and arrive at a different conclusion.
The trial of criminal cases and the evidence available in the criminal case has no bearing over adjudicating the claim petitions.

Ltd. Vs. Perhaps, as was the case before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, even here the eye witness was not examined and the Hon'ble High Court took note of the same.

Further in Vinayaka Dattatraya Naik Vs.Umesh Krishna Naik and another rendered by Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 103630/2016 (MV) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka was dealing with a scenario there it was alleged before the tribunal that the accident was caused by another vehicle but the medical records and discharge  SCCH-17 36 MVC 1320/2021 summary revealed that petitioner had informed the doctors that he had sustained injuries due to one unknown vehicle.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka took note of the said fact and considering the contradictory versions dismissed the petition.

Which is also the facts of this case in a nutshell because even Sunanda vs Renuka B Killari on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28063228/
24 here while registering the FIR only involvement of one vehicle is alleged but thereafter the story is cooked by implicating the motor cycle bearing No. KA-49-H-2462 along with one unknown vehicle.

36. To sum up it is relevant to note that advocate for respondent No.2 has argued that this is a false case which has been cooked up with the help of the deceased as the deceased also working in police department only to claim compensation in collusion with respondent No.1,
who is known to the petitioner and has supported the  SCCH-17 37 MVC 1320/2021 same by referring to Ex.P-12 and Ex.R-1 and 2 wherein it is stated that the accident is caused by one vehicle but thereafter the story is build up by showing the involvement of two vehicles.

The learned counsel for the petitioner has argued by relying on the judgments reported in  (2017) 16 SCC 680 between  National Insurance Company Limited  V/s. Pranay Sethi and Others,
 (2009) 6 SCC 121 between Sarla  Verma (SMT) And Others V/s.

Delhi  Transport Corporation and Another,
 37.

The learned counsel for the petitioners relied Sunanda vs Renuka B Killari on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28063228/
25 on the above quoted judgments by contending that the concept of preponderance of probabilities has to be  SCCH-17 38 MVC 1320/2021 applied and the heads to be considered while awarding compensation.

As discussed above, the petitioners failed to prove the involvement of the motor cycle bearing No.
KA-49-H-2462 in the accident even on the touch stone of legal theory of preponderance of probabilities.
Looking at any angle, no evidence is available to show the involvement of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-49-H- 2462 in the accident.
Per contra, the respondent No.2 sucessfully established their defence of non involvement of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-49-H-2462 in the accident.

38. As already observed, it is to be noted that it is well settled principle of law that the M.A.C.T Tribunal while deciding the point of negligence is not bound by conclusion arrived at by the IO and cannot accept the said conclusion as gospel truth, instead the tribunal is  SCCH-17 39 MVC 1320/2021 well within its jurisdiction in independently assessing the evidence to conclude whether there was rashness or negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and give a finding on the point of rash and negligence on the part of driver/driver of the offending vehicle without Sunanda vs Renuka B Killari on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28063228/
26 being influenced by the police papers and records of the criminal case instituted on the basis of such police investigation.

39. Where the burden cast on the petitioners was to prove that indeed the accident was caused by the motor cycle bearing No. KA-49-H-2462 which was manned by the respondent No.1 and thereby disprove the contention of the respondent No.2 that the deceased succumbed to the injuries, the fact that in none of the medical records or the evidence is available to show the involvement of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-49-H-  SCCH-17 40 MVC 1320/2021 2462.Thus this tribunal to holds that the petitioners have failed to discharge the burden cast on them in Issue No.1.
Wherefore Issue No.1 is answered in the negative.

ISSUE No.II:
 40.

In view of the above finding given by this court with respect to the Issue No.I, the question of determining entitlement of the petitioner for compensation as well as the determination of quantum of compensation would not arise at all.

In other words where the petitioner has failed to establish the very involvement of vehicle of respondent No.1, which was duly insured with respondent No.2 at the time of accident Sunanda vs Renuka B Killari on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28063228/
27 resulting in the death of Sri. Channagangaiah

hence,
there cannot be any second thought in holding that the  SCCH-17 41 MVC 1320/2021 petitioners are not entitled for any compensation.
Wherefore Issue No.II is also answered in the Negative.
ISSUE NO.3-  41.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs.
Draw the award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Channagangaiah, in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 12.2.2020.
On 12.2.2020 at about 5.30 p.m. the deceased Channagangaiah was coming out from Director General of Police office situated on Nrupathunga Road to reach his office, at that time the rider of bike bearing No. KA-49- H-2462 ridden the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased motor cycle.
Due to the impact the deceased sustained injuries and fell on the road, at the same time another motor bike deo vehicle which was also being ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
 Immediately after the accident the deceased was shifted to St. Martha's Hospital, Bengaluru wherein first aid treatment was given and later he was shifted to Sunanda vs Renuka B Killari on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28063228/
2 Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, but in spite of best  SCCH-17 4 MVC 1320/2021 treatment he succumbed to the said injuries on the same day.
At the time of accident, the deceased was working as Armed Head Constable in the police department and earning a sum of Rs.67,296/- p.m. and he was contributing the same to his family maintenance, but due to untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically.
The petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/-.
 3.
The accident had occurred due to negligence of the deceased himself.
Respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of insurance policy to the motor cycle bearing No. KA-49-H- 2462 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
The accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of deceased himself.
